Which of the following statements is false concerning the linear probability model?
Option A: There is nothing in the model to ensure that the estimated probabilities lie between zero and one
Option B: Even if the probabilities are truncated at zero and one, there will probably be many observations for which the probability is either exactly zero or exactly one
Option C: The error terms will be heteroscedastic and not normally distributed
Option D: The model is much harder to estimate than a standard regression model with a continuous dependent variable
